desc: Ideation complete: identify Fenwick-tree greedy/closed-form approaches and pitfalls.
Read the input and store the original 1-based position of each value in the permutation.
Implement a Fenwick tree supporting point updates and prefix-sum queries to count already removed larger values to the left of a given original position.

Iterate values v from N down to 1: query removed larger values before original_pos[v], compute current_pos = original_pos[v] - removed_left, and add the sum current_pos + ... + (v-1) if current_pos < v.
Update the Fenwick tree at original_pos[v] after processing v.
Use Python int for the answer, print the result, and check edge cases such as already sorted and reverse-sorted permutations.
Validate the implementation against the provided sample tests.
